page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6149 processor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 22 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1347.29, while the multi-core CPU performance reached 1787.79, positioning the instance in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 99.75 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 9.66 GB/sec. Geekbench evaluations yield a single-core score of 1064.0 and a multi-core score of 1258.0, reflecting limited processing capacity for demanding multi-threaded tasks.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest memory and compute footprint, the ecs.hfc5.large is suited for lightweight workloads. It can handle basic static web serving, which benchmarked at 1.4 GB/sec, and simple text processing tasks. However, it is not designed for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or modern machine learning workloads, as demonstrated by its low LLM inference speeds on small models and poor database operation scores. It represents a low-cost entry point for basic utility services, lightweight development environments, and simple background tasks where dedicated CPU access is required without high resource density.
